question: For sparse mixture-of-experts models adapted to reason in Greek, what stable behavioral changes do supervised fine-tuning and verifiable-reward RL produce when ordinary accuracy is dominated by training noise and evaluation artifacts?

key_findings.claim: Single-run accuracy differences are not resolvable at this scale, whereas reasoning language and trace length are much more stable under the same seed perturbation.
key_findings.evidence: Three otherwise identical Qwen LoRA runs score 76.2, 68.7, and 76.4, a 7.7-point range with estimated standard deviation 4.4 points; logic recall and answer fallback move with the failed seed. The same runs have Greek-trace fidelity 1.00/1.00/1.00 and median lengths 132/148/152 words. The authors estimate roughly 11 seeds per arm for a 6.3-point effect and 40 for a 3.2-point effect at 90% power using that variance estimate.

key_findings.claim: Language-matched SFT reliably changes the language of explicit reasoning traces without producing a corresponding accuracy gain.
key_findings.evidence: The measured base models produce 0 of 5,156 Greek-dominant traces on Greek questions, while the four released SFT checkpoints reach 97.4-98.1% Greek fidelity and retain 100% English traces on English controls. The pooled Greek reasoning benchmark does not show a fine-tuned model beating its own base; a headline comparison has identical 72.9% item-pooled accuracy while trace language and cost change sharply.

key_findings.claim: SFT makes reasoning effort track item difficulty and reduces words, but whether it reduces serving cost depends on each tokenizer's Greek fertility.
key_findings.evidence: In one matched probe the base uses a median 1,010 words per trace and 1,454 words per correct answer versus 150 and 239 for the reasoning-only fine-tune at equal accuracy. Across release families, median token use changes from 1,788 to 586 on Qwen, 681 to 638 on NemotronH, and 396 to 640 on Gpt-OSS because Greek uses 2.3-2.5 times as many tokens per word. Base overrun is 98.0% on easy items, versus 0.2-12% for fine-tunes.

key_findings.claim: Most apparent forgetting is an instrument or format effect; the consistent loss is answer-format compliance, while general ability and Greek grammar are largely retained or improved.
key_findings.evidence: A 12-of-12 commonsense deficit of -3.0 points reverses to +1.7 under a letter-only answer control. Qwen retention macros are flat (-0.01 Greek, +0.08 English); the format-repaired Gpt-OSS release is -3.2 Greek and +1.0 English; two Nemotron releases are +3.8/-2.0 and +1.7/-1.1. Judged grammaticality rises from 13/58 to 27/57 and 12/58 to 29/58 on the two weak Nemotron bases, and from 32/57 to 40/58 on Gpt-OSS. By contrast, requested-answer fallback can reach 24-26% on released checkpoints and 33-40% in two-phase training.

key_findings.claim: Reasoning-only SFT is the only accuracy recipe effect estimated over enough independent runs to survive the paper's noise floor, but its cross-family generality remains unresolved.
key_findings.evidence: Across 15 historical Qwen arms, reasoning-only training averages 73.6 over six runs versus 66.7 for two-phase training over nine, with 52 of 54 pairwise comparisons favoring it and exact permutation p=0.0008. A corpus-version-stratified permutation has only 16 valid assignments and p=0.125. On Gpt-OSS, one run per condition reverses the ordering, 62.5 versus 68.1.

key_findings.claim: Pre-registered RLVR repairs deterministic SFT defects while preserving the SFT-installed Greek reasoning habit, and the random-reward control attributes the repair to the reward rather than mere continuation.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen, correctness-plus-format-plus-termination reward reduces fallback from 24.1% to 2.5% and answer-channel leak from 3.53% to 0.00%, while random reward remains at 22.1% and 3.61%. Greek fidelity stays at 98.22%. Adding override reward moves Greek-question 'reason in English' compliance from 44.8% to 53.9%, versus 44.1% under random reward, but misses the preregistered 60% and +15-point threshold for calling the behavior trainable.

key_findings.claim: The study identifies six concrete instrument failures that materially changed or could have changed conclusions.
key_findings.evidence: The failures include an unanchored scorer producing a spurious +29.8-point effect, a 38.9%-contaminated logic probe, a model-family translation-register artifact of 3.1 standard deviations, Greek numeric separator errors, length-confounded repetition metrics, and a generation default that silently switched the intended thinking lane off. Each was caught by a targeted control or audit.

method.core_idea: Evaluate low-resource-language reasoning as a multi-dimensional behavioral adaptation problem, calibrate training variance before interpreting accuracy, and preregister deterministic controls for the remaining SFT defects.
method.mechanism: Four 3.6-4.0B-active-parameter sparse MoE checkpoints are adapted with rank-32 LoRA on 59,107 Greek reasoning rows paired with 58,985 direct instruction rows. The study measures anchored correctness, script fidelity, words and tokenizer tokens, termination, intermediate steps, item-conditioned budget overrun, fallback, channel leakage, and language switching across Greek generation, English controls, and direct-mode retention suites. Seed replicates establish an empirical accuracy floor. Language-matched SFT pairs Greek and English traces; a later preregistered GRPO round varies deterministic reward terms while holding prompts, data order, seed, hardware, and steps fixed and includes a random-reward control.
assumptions: Greek character share after removing code and LaTeX is an adequate automatic proxy for trace language, though not for trace quality or faithfulness.
The three-seed Qwen variance estimate is a useful warning threshold for other single-run comparisons, even though its numeric value is not measured on every model and recipe.
Active parameters per token are the relevant size axis for comparing sparse MoE deployment cost.
Anchored answer extraction, target-language numeric parsing, and the chosen direct-mode retention suite isolate format behavior from capability better than raw benchmark accuracy.
A random-reward GRPO arm with identical execution is a valid control for continuation, sampling, and model-family elicitation effects.

techniques.role: Repeats one configuration with only initialization and shuffle seed changed before interpreting ablation-sized accuracy deltas.
Scores the requested final line before any fallback parser and reports how often that line is absent.
Measures whether a reasoning trace uses Greek after stripping code and mathematical notation that would otherwise inflate Latin characters.
Flags traces at least three times longer than the across-arm median for items at least 80% of arms solve, separating waste from difficulty.
Places each question beside a trace in the same language, retaining both Greek and English support rather than training one output direction.
Adds a small set of trace-less anchored answer-closing examples to repair response termination without replacing the reasoning corpus.
Tests deterministic RL rewards against filler, answer sprays, code laundering, locale exploits, truncation, and instruction-disobedience cases before optimization.
Runs the same GRPO steps and prompts with random scalar feedback so a trained-arm change is attributable to reward information.

evaluations.setting: Qwen reasoning-only LoRA, three seeds, fixed 1,000-item Greek probe
evaluations.metric: Three-axis mean accuracy, logic recall, fallback, trace Greek
evaluations.result: Means 76.2/68.7/76.4; logic 56.2/35.6/54.0; fallback 10%/41%/3%; trace Greek 1.00 for all
evaluations.baseline: Identical data, recipe, step count, and greedy decoding

evaluations.setting: Full 5,156-item Greek reasoning benchmark across four released SFT checkpoints
evaluations.metric: Fraction of traces with Greek-character ratio at least 0.9
evaluations.baseline: Measured Qwen and Gpt-OSS bases 0.0%; every measured fine-tune remains 100% English on English controls

evaluations.result: Qwen 1,788 to 586; NemotronH 681 to 638; Gpt-OSS 396 to 640
evaluations.baseline: Each released fine-tune versus its own base; Greek token fertility is 2.3-2.5 times English

evaluations.setting: Fifteen independently trained historical Qwen arms
evaluations.baseline: Corpus-version-stratified permutation p=0.125 with only 16 valid permutations

evaluations.metric: Greek/English macro change from each base
evaluations.result: Qwen -0.01/+0.08; repaired Gpt-OSS -3.2/+1.0; Nemotron Nano +3.8/-2.0; Lightning +1.7/-1.1
evaluations.baseline: Nine Greek and five English frozen benchmarks, log-likelihood scoring without generated traces

evaluations.setting: Preregistered Qwen RLVR, 2,000 prompts, 8 samples per prompt, one seed per arm
evaluations.metric: Fallback, answer leak, Greek fidelity, override compliance
evaluations.result: Plain RLVR 2.5% fallback, 0.00% leak, 98.22% fidelity; override arm 53.9% Greek-question-to-English compliance

limitations: Author-stated: every model is a sparse MoE and every adaptation uses LoRA, so the findings do not establish behavior for dense models or full fine-tuning.
Author-stated: most configurations have one seed; the main noise estimate uses n=3 on one Qwen arm and is transferred qualitatively, not numerically, to other families.
Author-stated: LoRA rank, target stride, epoch count, and greedy decoding are fixed rather than ablated.
Author-stated: Greek is mid-resource with dedicated base models; transfer to genuinely low-resource languages is untested.

Author-stated: almost all trace-language evaluation is automatic script identity, not human-rated fluency, terminology, followability, or causal faithfulness; the hand switching probe has one annotator and no agreement measure.
Author-stated: post-hoc trace translation and few-shot Greek-trace prompting are not compared, and the zero-switch criterion may penalize legitimate Greek technical borrowing.

Reviewer-identified: the reasoning-only versus two-phase result aggregates historical arms with incompletely balanced corpus versions, so its strong unstratified p-value is not equivalent to a designed randomized replication.
Reviewer-identified: the RLVR result is one Qwen seed and one short prompt pool; it is an existence proof with a strong control, not a robust recipe estimate.
failure_modes: A scorer that searches free text instead of the requested final field can penalize longer, more explicit reasoning and manufacture large accuracy differences.
Translated evaluation items can share a generator's linguistic register with training traces, preferentially advantaging the fine-tuned model without literal contamination.
Locale-insensitive numeric parsing can score correct target-language numbers as wrong and wrong decimal forms as correct.
Mixing trace-bearing and direct rows in one phase can collapse the requested reasoning switch; a second hybrid phase can instead damage answer closing.
One-directional language SFT can suppress explicit language-override instructions even while preserving English-on-English default behavior.
Tokenizer fertility can reverse a word-level efficiency conclusion when translated into billed tokens.
MoE routing and LoRA initialization can create occasional low-performing seeds whose benchmark drop looks like a data or method effect.
Reward code can silently omit an instruction field or reward fluent filler unless adversarial tests and run-time assertions verify every term receives its intended inputs.
reusable_insights: Run a repeat-seed control before expensive ablations; the variance of doing nothing is the reference distribution for every claimed intervention.
Treat accuracy as one behavioral coordinate, not a sufficient summary, when fine-tuning targets language, style, cost, routing, or compliance.
Always report requested-format fallback beside task accuracy so inability and unwillingness to close in the expected form remain separable.
Measure both words and tokenizer tokens in cross-language efficiency studies; only the latter represents serving cost, while the former is the language-fair effort unit.
Build translated benchmarks with a human-translated holdout and contamination checks in both source and target languages.
Preregister reward gates and null branches, fuzz deterministic rewards, and include random-reward controls before interpreting RLVR changes.
Test trace-language steerability per checkpoint; matched default behavior does not imply explicit override compliance.
open_questions: Does sparse expert routing amplify seed sensitivity relative to a capacity-matched dense model under the same LoRA recipe?
Why does identical language-matched SFT reopen the English override channel on Qwen and Gpt-OSS but not on either Nemotron checkpoint?
Can a larger, multi-seed RLVR study cross the preregistered override trainability threshold without degrading either language direction?
Do human readers find Greek traces more auditable and useful, and are the traces faithful to the computation that produced the answer?
Can few-shot native-language traces or post-hoc translation deliver comparable auditability at lower training and serving cost?
Which curriculum preserves both direct and reasoning modes while avoiding the answer-format tax observed in hybrid phases?

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models are Multilingual Chain-of-Thought Reasoners
competitive_landscape.difference: Shi et al. introduce MGSM and show multilingual CoT prompting improves with scale, primarily evaluating answer performance across ten languages. This paper treats trace language, cost, termination, format, retention, and steerability as separate targets and studies weight adaptation rather than prompting alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Multilingual Language Models Think Better in English?
competitive_landscape.difference: Etxaniz et al. find self-translation to English improves multilingual task accuracy and treats English as a useful pivot. This paper adopts a deployment objective in which native-language reasoning is itself the product, finds a controlled trace-language accuracy effect collapses, and quantifies the native trace's cost and steerability.

competitive_landscape.title: Cross-lingual Collapse: How Language-Centric Foundation Models Shape Reasoning in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. show GRPO can rapidly revert low-resource reasoning to the dominant pretraining language and that consistency rewards cost 5-10 accuracy points. Here SFT first installs question-matched Greek reasoning, and a small controlled RLVR round preserves about 98.2% fidelity even without a language term while repairing format and leak defects.

competitive_landscape.title: Think Natively: Unlocking Multilingual Reasoning with Consistency-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: M-Thinker uses GRPO language-consistency and cross-lingual alignment rewards to jointly improve accuracy and nearly eliminate language drift. This paper uses SFT for the default reasoning language, then isolates what a short verifier-only RL stage fixes with preregistered behavioral thresholds and a random-reward control.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Test-time Compute for Low-resource Languages: Multilingual Reasoning in LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: Tran et al. deliberately train English-pivoted CoT because it improves low-resource-language answer performance. This paper optimizes for readable native-language traces even when accuracy is flat, making auditability and serving economics explicit deployment objectives rather than treating English reasoning as the default optimum.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the work is a controlled multi-family study of what Greek reasoning SFT changes beyond accuracy, together with a preregistered RLVR repair of SFT-induced format and channel defects. Primary multilingual-CoT and consistency-RL papers already study native versus English reasoning, language drift, and consistency rewards. Reviewer inference: the strongest novelty is methodological—the seed floor, six-dimensional behavior panel, failure log, locale-aware controls, explicit SFT-versus-RL division of labor, and random-reward-controlled repair—not the existence of multilingual reasoning adaptation itself. The breadth of controls is unusually valuable, but the central accuracy null and RL repair remain limited by few seeds, MoE-only models, and one language.
reviewer_notes: All reported numbers were checked against page-marked Tables 4, 6-16 and the surrounding caveats. The paper is unusually explicit about withdrawn findings; those corrections are treated as results about measurement, not evidence that every retained causal interpretation is proven. Primary arXiv records verify the competitive papers and their stated mechanisms.
